video_title: SPECIAL EDITION: What The Knicks Mean To NYC & This Epic NBA Finals Run

quotes.speaker: Mike Walciewski
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Walciewski on the Knicks' performance in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I think everybody will say it's just been beautiful basketball to watch for the last month and a half.
quotes.quote: I've been to a lot of games at the Garden and I've wanted to do a show in New York City for a long time, and it's pretty cool to be in New York City doing a live show at the Gotham Comedy Club and having Mike Walciewski introduce us. That is a pretty awesome thing. This season has been wonderful, and it's been a sneaky season because the team started out a good team, but then a couple of months ago, it just went into a different gear. The connectivity was great, the ball movement was great, the players were just meshing very, very well. And once we got into the playoffs, especially once we got past those first game or two, it was shining. I mean it was great, it was beautiful. And I think everybody will say it's just been beautiful basketball to watch for the last month and a half.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert on the physical toll of the NBA season
quotes.excerpt: I had to take the point guard load on where my body was still adjusting to the league.
quotes.quote: For me, I found out a lot about myself because if you remember, for most of the year, I had to take the point guard load on where my body was still adjusting to the league. I didn't really know what it was like to play this many games and then it was also done at a time during the lockout. So we had a game every day, sometimes four games, five nights and my body had never been through that. People were dropping like flies, but I just remember going through that and being exhausted in that Nets game. I had to guard D-Rose, then Rondo, then Darren Williams. So I was like, my body just, I remember that game, me and Darren Williams looking at each other and I'm like, almost talking to him like with my eyes like, dog, get off the ball. Pass it. So I got nothing left.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert on playing through injuries in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I had an MCL sprain early that season and Jalen Brunson is how I got back in shape.
quotes.quote: They didn't realize I had an MCL sprain early that season and Jalen Brunson is how I got back in shape and got back right. Me and Jalen Brunson were playing one-on-one full court. We were doing a lot of stuff, drilling stuff in the half court, but me and Jalen Brunson almost could predict each other's moves. So I kind of knew like, though he's got energy, shorty got game. I like, nobody knows he got game and a little bit of swagger with it. So reminding him of, you know, the Kobe game, you know, those atmospheres like, that Kobe game, that Kobe game, I mean I was at that game, that was one of the craziest games I've ever been at.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on players managing injuries in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: In the NBA, everybody's hurt. You can't play these Finals games. I mean, y'all saw it.
quotes.quote: People underestimate, in the NBA, everybody's hurt. You can't play these Finals games. I mean, y'all saw it. Y'all saw Jalen Williams get thrown. You know what I'm saying? Then he got, y'all saw it. Y'all saw him get thrown. I saw him flop. I saw him flop. Listen, I was sitting in the second level and I looked down at the court and I literally saw courtside, I said, 'Oh, there's Jalen Williams, right there. I can see him from a half a mile away.'

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on the Spurs' young talent and team culture
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs are young, a bunch of young guys still figuring it out, but they're also like a sense of gratitude.
quotes.quote: The Spurs are young, a bunch of young guys still figuring it out, but they're also like a sense of gratitude with these guys. Like, 'Man, we are here right now,' and they can't believe it, but they realize that they have to be in the moment. So like, I think the feeling is that, 'Hey, we're going to be here a lot of times moving forward.' So we'll see how that goes for them. You get the privilege of getting to see Victor Wembanyama up close every day for us as our Spurs guy. And obviously everybody here is seeing him in the Finals, is watching him in this playoff run. But what does it been like being around that guy on a daily basis and seeing sort of what the whole show is up close on a regular basis?

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on Victor Wembanyama's maturity and focus
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama is introspective, thoughtful guy. Like, today, he was talking about things he's learned in the playoffs.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama is introspective, thoughtful guy. Like, today, he was talking about things he's learned in the playoffs and he was like, 'I learned that, uh, if you're going to elbow somebody, don't go for the head.' He also said, 'Brace with your hands, not with your chin when you fall.' Yeah, like, so like, that's Victor, though. Like, I wish, like today he was so engaged and like, that's the Victor I like to see. But sometimes like, Victor gets into those modes where like, 'Okay, I'm ultra-focused, I don't have time for the media, I'm all about, you know, trying to help the Spurs get to the next step.' And sometimes that's boring to me.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on Victor Wembanyama's physical play
quotes.excerpt: The way he spends his energy, it's like the whole tank is empty. Like, it's because he's going hard.
quotes.quote: The way he spends his energy, it's like the whole tank is empty. Like, it's because he's going hard on both ends of the floor. He's going to guard the other team's best guy, and he's going to guard them in a physical way that, that, you know, just wears him out. And handle the ball, too. And handle the ball. I mean, but the turnovers have been an issue for him. When they drafted Castle two years ago, so you remember this draft two years ago, it was the draft in between Wembanyama and Cooper Flagg. I mean, they're good players, but, you know, Zachary Risacher went number one to Atlanta, Alex Sarr went number two to Washington, two French guys. Number three, Reed Sheppard to Houston. That's going to haunt the Rockets, for sure. Emoni Bates, I think he'd like Stefan Castle. And, uh, and who, they had a chance to take, uh, Donovan Clingan went after that. Anyway, the Spurs take, take Castle. And I was talking to one of their front office guys, like, two weeks later. They're like, 'We got him.' I'm like, 'Uh, what do you got?' 'We got Victor's running mate.' And I'm like, 'He's been here for two weeks.'

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' decision to bench Rudy Gobert against Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: They have this guy who is the best defensive player in the league and they took him off
quotes.quote: They have this guy who is the best defensive player in the league and they took him off the tallest player in the NBA. I think he's a legit 7'6". Anyway, forget about all that. They have this guy who is the best defensive player in the league and they got together and they were like, listen man, he can't guard Karl-Anthony Towns. We better take him off. Karl-Anthony Towns forced them to take Wembanyama off him. He should have been, the way he was beating his chest at the end of Game 2, when he came out and saw that alignment on defense, he should have been like, 'I'll be goddamned.' They took him off me.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks need a reality check after their recent playoff struggles
quotes.excerpt: I just think the Knicks need a reality check sometimes. The playoffs are supposed to be a struggle.
quotes.quote: I just think the Knicks need a reality check sometimes. The playoffs are supposed to be a struggle. The Knicks have made everything from whatever that day was in April where CJ McCollum was lighting you guys up, that seemed like two years ago. The playoffs are so damn long, but that was so long ago and you blew through Philly who was toothless, you blew through Cleveland who was heartless, and I think sometimes it got a little too easy.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown's coaching style and his ability to make adjustments
quotes.excerpt: Mike Brown is humble and he's self-deprecating and sometimes he's goofy. But the guy has won a lot.
quotes.quote: I've known Mike Brown for 20 years and Mike Brown is humble and he's self-deprecating and sometimes he's goofy. But the guy has won a lot and one thing Mike Brown has done throughout his career is in playoff series, he makes adjustments that work. We've seen it so far this playoffs, he makes adjustments that work.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's performance and the Spurs' defensive strategy
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson hasn't had a game yet this series. He had a quarter.
quotes.quote: Jalen Brunson hasn't had a game yet this series. He had a quarter. Now, I think the Spurs, I wouldn't want Stephen Curry to castle garden me either because you said he had Shay in hell, he got Jalen Brunson in the gates of hell. That's real. But I do think Carl lives the lever and there's no way in hell that OG Anunoby has 28 points last night on 13 shots. He's the guy that you have to unlock. You have so many different weapons, you can take Jalen Brunson off the ball and still use him as a weapon.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' expectation to win the series against the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: The expectation should be we win this series. And if you don't, a lot of people are going to be on your ass.
quotes.quote: The expectation should be we win this series. And if you don't, more than Stephen, they're going to be on your ass. A lot of people are going to be on the Knicks' ass. You should win tomorrow, bottom line. You discovered Karl-Anthony Towns, you discovered Jalen Brunson, you should win tomorrow. But baby, if you don't, we're going back to Texas.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Predictions for the next two games of the series
quotes.excerpt: Probably what's going to happen is they're going to split the next two games.
quotes.quote: Probably what's going to happen is they're going to split the next two games. And I don't know, because nobody wins at home anymore in the NBA. I don't know. And then six is going to be here next week for all the marbles. That's what's going to happen.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' need to match the Spurs' physicality
quotes.excerpt: I wonder, my fear for Knicks fans is that will the Knicks match San Antonio's physicality?
quotes.quote: I wonder, my fear for Knicks fans is that will the Knicks match San Antonio's physicality? Because the Spurs don't scare. Did y'all see the way they were putting Karl-Anthony Towns on his ass yesterday, Jalen Brunson on his ass? A couple of flops, but they put Jalen Brunson on his ass yesterday. They have brought a level of physicality that's only going to ramp up as the series goes on. So, if I'm the Knicks, that's what I'm concerned about is, do you have the requisite physicality to match what the Spurs are going to bring you?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of the playoffs and the lasting memories they create
quotes.excerpt: You don't want a simple playoff series. You want a playoff series to remember.
quotes.quote: The whole NBA is this type of situation. You want this stress. This is what you want. You don't want a simple playoff series. You want a playoff series to remember. And this, you guys are all going to remember these two months. These two months are going to be some, you're going to be talking about them in 10 or 15 years. And I just want you to know that I'm so happy that this week that you're going to remember for the next 15 or 20 years, that we could be a little part of it and that you could come out and enjoy it with us.
